synopsis: Sensor requirements vary by acceptance regime: MOSH specifies a minimum 200 m surface machine-to-machine detection range and range accuracy of 1.5 m or 10%, while the cited US construction rules prescribe neither a numeric range nor automatic braking [f2605, f2114, f2765]. The booklet derives required detection range backwards from stopping distance and treats sensing cadence as part of braking delay: at 15 km/h and 10 FPS, each extra confirmation frame adds about 0.4 m of travel before braking [f12545, f13921]. Coverage depends on mounting geometry and self-occlusion, so moving a sensor can invalidate correlation; variants inside the validated parameter hull should receive reduced physical checks covering brake calibration, field of view and detection at the new mount [f5601, f1997, f7917]. Weather-dependent range needs physical evidence: 2023 on-road measurements found aluminium and steel targets unobserved at 20–30 m in specified rain and fog conditions, while fog chambers limited to, for example, 30 m require extrapolation of long-range behaviour [f6382, f4652]. Simulation and stimulation have important limitations: hardware-in-the-loop constrains distance and field of view, reported radar minimum ranges differ between a 2021 review's 20–30 m and vendor claims of 0.6 m partly because architectures differ, and actual sensor workloads require benchmarking rather than an assumed real-time factor [f4437, f5777, f8874]. Comparisons should use a common stopping-distance or risk-based evaluation zone rather than native sensor fields of view, because coverage outside their overlap is not directly comparable; KomVision's numerical travel speeds and detection ranges remain unreported in the supplied findings [f5479, f5484, f1643].
